title: larrea tridentata var. glutinosa
intro: Larrea tridentata var. glutinosa, commonly known as chaparral or creosote bush, is a shrub native to the southwestern United States and northern Mexico. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The therapeutic actions of Larrea tridentata var. glutinosa include wound healing, immune system support, and protection against oxidative stress. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and diterpenes, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
